# Parivattanahāravibhaṅga (Ne 12)

**ID:** Ne 12
**Section:** Netti (ne)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Parivattanahāravibhaṅga
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0519m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Parivattanahāravibhaṅga* ("Conveying a Reversal: Analysis") constitutes the twelfth division (Ne 12) of the *Nettippakaraṇa*. In modern scholarship, Giuliana Martini cites Ne 12 (occurring at PTS Nett 65) for its exposition of the two types of reliance or dependence (*nissaya*): reliance on craving (*taṇhānissaya*) and reliance on views (*diṭṭhinissaya*) [Martini]. The passage analyzes how intentions conditioned by attachment or delusion act as volitional formations (*saṅkhārā*) that give rise to the full sequence of dependent arising (*paṭiccasamuppāda*) [Martini].

**Sources**

- [Martini] Giuliana Martini (Dhammadinna), Semantics of Wholesomeness: Purification of Intention and the Soteriological Function of the Immeasurables (appamaṇas) in Early Buddhist Thought — Discussed Ne 12 at PTS Nett 65 regarding the two types of nissaya and paṭiccasamuppāda.
